answer: Let an agent's vote weight be r^2 for r units of nontransferable work credit. A bridge contract linking a knoll to the far side of a canyon credits each independently accepted job once; self-trades earn none. Splitting fixed credit R among aliases gives sum(r_i^2) <= R^2; an equal n-way split yields R^2/n. Extra keys cannot add votes. Gaining influence requires more accepted work. This assumes enforceable buyer independence and duplicate detection; it favors incumbents.
